turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hey, Marcus here. You’ve got about twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. Can I spend two minutes understanding where your seven-month ramp is driving rep attrition, then we’ll decide whether this is relevant?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sure, but to be precise, seven months is time to first closed deal. I didn’t say it was driving attrition.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair correction. Walk me through what happens between a new AE’s start date and that first closed deal at month seven.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: First month is product training, shadowing, and mock calls; then they start building pipeline. Deals tend to stall in technical validation because reps fumble integration questions and pull in an engineer too late.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How often do deals stall in technical validation, and what does bringing engineers in late cost in engineering time or delayed revenue?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We don’t track it cleanly, but Rachel estimates roughly a third of technical validations need rescuing. That pulls an engineer into one or two calls a week; I can’t give you a credible delayed-revenue number.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s enough to baseline the load. In a typical month, how many engineering hours go to rescues, and how many validations still fail?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Call it eight to twelve engineering hours a month. We don’t track how many validations still fail after the rescue.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: When those rescues happen, which integration questions are reps fumbling, and why aren’t the month-one mock calls preparing them?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly API authentication, webhook failure handling, ERP edge cases, and data residency. The mock calls are generic; managers don’t consistently play a technical buyer or push on follow-up questions.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How many new AEs go through this annually, and how much manager time is spent running mocks and assessing technical readiness?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Four or five new AEs in a typical year. I don’t have a reliable number on manager time; Rachel would, but the mocks are fairly ad hoc.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: If Rachel could verify technical readiness before live calls, what would need to improve in the seven-month ramp and those eight-to-twelve rescue hours?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I’d want time to first deal moving from seven months toward five, and engineering rescue time cut at least in half. I wouldn’t assume readiness alone gets us there, but those would be meaningful outcomes.
